blocks.text: וּבְכֵן דַּיַּן אֱמֶת אָֽתָּה׃
uncertainties: The pointing on the second word is hard to read. It looks like patach+dagesh under dalet, then yod with patach, then final nun (דַּיַּן). The expected form is דַּיָּן with qamats, but there is a mark under the yod that might be a cantillation or accent sign. Treat this word as uncertain.
It is unclear whether the vertical stroke under aleph in אָֽתָּה is a meteg.

blocks.text: פותחים הארון.
חזן.
ע״ם א״ב.
uncertainties: The second letter in the small print could be final mem (ע״ם) or samekh (ע״ס). The intended reading is probably ע״ס א״ב (על סדר אלף בית). The text above records the letter as it appears.

blocks.text: קהל.
לְאֵל עוֹרֵךְ דִּין׃ לְבוֹחֵן לְבָבוֹת בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
לְגוֹלֶה עֲמוּקוֹת בַּדִּין׃ לְדוֹבֵר מֵישָׁרִים בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
לְהוֹגֶה דֵעוֹת בַּדִּין׃ לְוָתִיק וְעֹשֶׂה חֶסֶד בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
uncertainties: The left half is tightly set, with little or no space between words (looks like לְוָתִיקוְעֹשֶׂהחֶסֶד). The word breaks above are inferred.
It is unclear whether וְעֹשֶׂה is defective (holam over ayin) or plene וְעוֹשֶׂה. The scan looks defective.
There is a small mark over ה in לְהוֹגֶה. It may be a meteg, an accent, or a print speck.

blocks.text: לְזוֹכֵר בְּרִיתוֹ בַּדִּין׃ לְחוֹמֵל מַעֲשָׂיו בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
לְטַהֵר חוֹסָיו בַּדִּין׃ לְיוֹדֵעַ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
uncertainties: The first letter of the last word in the right half looks somewhat like kaf (כַּדִּין) and not bet. The expected reading is בַּדִּין. If it is kaf, it is a print artifact or a source typo; proposed correction: בַּדִּין.
The pointing of שָׁ in מַחֲשָׁבוֹת is partly obscured by a mark above the shin.

blocks.text: לְכוֹבֵשׁ כַּעְסוֹ בַּדִּין׃ לְלוֹבֵשׁ צְדָקוֹת בְּיוֹם דִּין׃
uncertainties: As in row 05, the first letter of the last word in the right half could be read as kaf (כַּדִּין). The expected reading is בַּדִּין.
There is a possible meteg or other small mark in כַּעְסוֹ.

blocks.text: ובכן
And thus Thou art the true judge.
לאל
God who arranges judgment, Who examines hearts on the day of judgment,
Who reveals secrets in judgment, Who speaks uprightness on the day of judgment,
Who considers opinions in judgment, Who in knowledge acts kindly on the day of judgment,
Who remembers His covenant in judgment, Who pities His creatures on the day of judgment,
Who cleanses those who trust in Him, in judgment, Who knows thoughts on the day of judgment,
Who suppresses His anger in judgment, Who clothes Himself in righteousness on the day of judgment,

notes: As instructed, all Adirei Ayummah material above ובכן on s144 and above 'And thus Thou art the true judge' on s145 is left out.

Lael Orekh Din is set in two columns. The right column is marked חזן. and the left column קהל. Each row joins the right-column phrase with the left-column phrase on the same line. On s145 the English is laid out the same way: left column, then right column. Hyphenated line-breaks in the English (judg-ment, cove-nant, kind-ly, right-eousness) are rejoined above.
The rows go through the alphabet in pairs (א/ב through כ/ל) and continue past the bottom of both scans. Both pages end at row כ/ל.
There are no Psalm or other Biblical citations, and no attributions, on the parts of these pages I was assigned.
On s144 there is no cantillation in the transcribed section. All marks are vowel points plus a few possible meteg/accent strokes, flagged per block.
The bands overlap the full pages. Seams were checked against the full images, and each line appears once.
The s145 English rubric does not translate פותחים הארון / חזן / קהל / ע״ם א״ב, so no English rubric blocks were added.
